source: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise (https://attack.mitre.org). IDs, names and tactics from ATT&CK; descriptions are SentinelX summaries, not MITRE text.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Repeated authentication attempts to guess or reuse credentials when the password is unknown.

techniques.name: Password Guessing
techniques.description: Many password attempts against one or a few accounts, typically visible as bursts of failed logins.

techniques.name: Password Spraying
techniques.description: A small set of common passwords tried across many accounts to avoid per-account lockouts.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Use of legitimate credentials, for example a successful login after guessing, to gain or keep access.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Abuse of command shells or script interpreters to execute commands.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: Use of PowerShell for execution, often with encoded commands or download cradles.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.description: Enumeration of files and directories to locate information of interest.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.description: Collection of sensitive files from the local system before exfiltration.

techniques.name: Data from Network Shared Drive
techniques.description: Collection of sensitive files from network shares accessible to the compromised account.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.description: Exploitation of a software vulnerability to obtain higher privileges.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
techniques.description: Bypassing or abusing elevation controls such as UAC or sudo to run with higher privileges.
